events.text: The Alliance of Freesailors is formally disbanded, swelling ranks in the Cormyrean Imperial Navy.
Sembia becomes entirely absorbed by Netheril.
Krehlan Arunsun takes on the role of Blackstaff of Waterdeep.
After Bryseis Kakistos turns against Asmodeus, she gives the Old Staff to Caisys the Vicelord to hide it so Asmodeus cannot use Azuth's powers to the fullest.
Caisys the Vicelord hides the Old Staff in a cave of the Dead Stone Mountains, on the continent of Shyr.
The Devil You Know: Bryseis Kakistos's story, part nine.

The island of Snowdown in the Moonshae Isles comes under the control of Amn. This annexation comes after a slow but steady consolidation of power on the island as well as a civil war against the Kendrick Dynasty believed to have been supported by Amn.
The city of Proskur is annexed by the Kingdom of Cormyr.
Emvar Obarskyr, first son of King Azoun V and Queen Nalara Marliir of Cormyr.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: High Queen Alicia Kendrick of the Moonshaes dies unexpectedly, sending the realm into turmoil. It is commonly believed that she was poisoned by agents of Lionel Carrathal, the heir to the former Carrathal Dynasty who claims to be the "true" High King.
cites: Dragon 405: Heroes of the Moonshaes, с. 5

events.text: Following High Queen Alicia's death, supporters of Lionel Carrathal begin an insurgency in Callidyrr. They are defeated by the newly formed Callidyrr dragoons.
cites: Dragon 405: Heroes of the Moonshaes, с. 5

events.text: After several efforts to dislodge Amnian forces from Caer Westphal, House Kendrick fails to regain control of the island of Snowdown.
cites: Dragon 405: Heroes of the Moonshaes, с. 5

events.text: The Cormaeril family rebuilds Castle Daggerdale.

After a rumour arises that the Haunted Halls of Eveningstar has been cleared of danger, twelve adventuring companies disappear trying to loot its treasures. Entry into the famous dungeon is banned by the crown without a royal warrant.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: Urmlaspyr declares itself an ally of Cormyr.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: Branwyn Moonsinger, granddaughter of High Queen Alicia Kendrick of the Moonshae Isles and future Great Druid, is born.
The Devil You Know Bryseis Kakistos story, part ten.
Bruenor Battlehammer fakes his own death in order to secretly abdicate the throne of Mithral Hall, making Banak Brawnanvil the new king.
Azoun V and Nalara Marliir give birth to Foril Obarskyr, future king of Cormyr.
Obould Many-Arrows dies peacefully of old age in comfort.
A draconic plague rips through the metallic dragons of the Copper Mountains, sending survivors south to seek refuge in Murghôm and other nations.
A massive blizzard pelts the region around Castle Vathar. Refugees from the surrounding regions take refuge in the fortress until the weather clears.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 58

events.text: One of the survivors of the draconic plague in the Copper Mountains, Skalnaedyr, becomes the first of the Dragon Princes of Murghôm.
Urlgen becomes king of Many-Arrows, taking his father's name of Obould to become Obould II.
The Beloved Ranger, a statue in honor of Minsc and Boo, is erected in Baldur's Gate.
cites: Murder in Baldur's Gate: Campaign Guide, с. 13

events.text: Gauntlgrym (prologue)

Following years of steady expansion by the fey of Sarifal into the territory of Corwell on the Isle of Gwynneth, an attack by Amnian mercenaries results in Corwell being put to the torch, prompting High Lady Ordalf to expel the remaining Ffolk from the isle.
Shakti becomes Matron Mother of House Hunzrin and begins exerting control over the day-to-day essential resources of Menzoberranzan.
Those members of House Cormaeril who remain loyal to the throne of Cormyr are restored to that nation's nobility.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: Krehlan Arunsun and the Grand Mages of Rhymanthiin dissipated the kiira n'vaelhar which once held the spirits and combined knowledge of the first three Blackstaffs, and bounded its magic to Blackstaff Tower and its twin in Rhymanthiin, N’Vaerymanth.
Featherdale is 'accidentally conquered' by the Shadovar of Netheril after years of Sembian investors buying up most of its economy.
An adventuring company exploring Old Shanatar discovers Xenfyrth's Abyss; only Xenfyrth survives.

Young Prince Foril I of Cormyr falls gravely ill and the Shou noble Duc-Sum Li is the only person able to heal him. In gratitude, King Azoun V grants Duc-Sum land in Marsember which becomes the Shou district of Xiousing.
Unable to subvert their neighbor as bloodlessly as they Featherdale, Sembian mercenaries out of Yhaunn overrun Tasseldale.
The Zhentarim's quest to take over for Daggerdale begins anew. The cleric of Bane Rezlus begins operating out of the Mines of Tethyamar where the Tower of the Void is located.
Members of House Alsevir, a noble house of Cormyr long thought extinct, return to Suzail and take up residence in the old Bleth estate.

Scardale falls to Sembia when a mercenary army sacks Chandlerscross, slaughtering or driving off the inhabitants. This comes after a long series of betrayals, underhanded dealings, and consolidations of power that undermined Scardale. With Chandlerscross destroyed, the capital of Scardale moves to Scardale Town.
The Filthy Oar is lost at sea with all hands.
Battledale comes under heavy attack by forces from Netheril and Sembia for its embargoes against its puppet states, forcing the evacuation of Essembra.
Purple Dragon Knights of Cormyr move into High Dale to stave off Sembian advances upon their land.
The city of Elversult becomes a Cormyrean protectorate.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: An accidental explosion in the platinum mine of Vermeillon causes the deaths or disappearances of forty-nine miners. Following this, a slew of mysterious disappearances plagues the village until most of its residents flee.
cites: Candlekeep Mysteries: A Deep and Creeping Darkness, с. 49

events.text: The volcano Mount Kolimnis in the central Aphrunn Mountains erupts violently, burying Gildenglade in Turmish under hundreds of feet of ash and mud.
The remote duchy of Velen secedes from Tethyr after it is cut off from the rest of civilization by the rise of the monstrous nation of Muranndin.
Velen in Tethyr becomes an independent duchy.
Kamoth Kastelmar is born.
Chartham Dellenvol kills the Blackstaff, Krehlan Arunsun. His long-time friend and heir, Ashemmon, declares himself the new Blackstaff.
The Simbul disappears from Aglarond. A civil war erupts as soon as the news spreads with various groups trying to gain power over the country.
Velsharoon is engulfed in flames and perishes. His body is eventually secured by the people of Aglarond.
The Dales Compact is renewed in Mistledale between the Dalelands and Myth Drannor, and the Standing Stone is restored.
The Seven Burghers of Harrowdale strike a formal alliance with Myth Drannor, with Harrowdale Town being renamed New Velar in commemoration.
Teziir, the final free port on the shores of the Dragonmere, becomes part of Cormyr.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: The Abolethic Sovereignty attacks Akanûl and destroys the city of Brassune before the genasi could mount a proper defense to repel the aboleths from their country.
Families of the Twelvefold join forces for the first time in their history to attack and destroy Darkturret, to take revenge on the Garrandar family.
Members of the Garrandar family commission the construction of Darkturret, a castle fortress were they hide wealth stolen from other Twelvefold families.
The traveling wizard Rucksam creates a tunnel near the village of Rothé Valley in order to win a bet against farmer Fergus Gunderson. The tunnel is dubbed "Rucksam Tunnel" in remembrance of the bet.
Foril Obarskyr and Jemra Rhindaun, niece to Queen Sybille of Tethyr, wed.
Jemra Rhindaun gives birth to a healthy Irvel Obarskyr, son of Foril Obarskyr.
The surface elves living in the sea elf settlement of Naramyr abandon their homes and move back to their ancestral homes in Myth Drannor.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: Having lost his family, his title, and most of his army, Lord Vanrak Moonstar renounces his faith in Shar and begs Selûne for forgiveness for his past crimes—particularly the slaughter he committed in the High House of Stars in 1182 DR. In a desperate act of redemption, he commits suicide with a sun blade.
cites: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage, с. 232

events.text: After Vanrak's suicide, Keresta Delvingstone, a vampire cleric of Shar, takes control of Vanrakdoom, its remaining cultists, and Umbraxakar the shadow dragon.
cites: Waterdeep: Dungeon of the Mad Mage, с. 232

events.text: An unnatural miasma blots out the sun in a number of Cormyrean towns along the border with Sembia.
Crown Prince Emvar Obarskyr dies in an ambush by Sembian forces south of the Vast Swamp.
Jemra Rhindaun is killed in a failed assassination attempt on Azoun V.

Ganrahast discovers that Emvar Obarskyr has a son fathered on a commoner named Solatha Boldtree. Solatha is made Countess of Dhedluk by Azoun V so his grandson Erzoured Obarskyr might have a title to inherit.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: A series of battles between Cormyr and Sembia lead to a full-scale war.
Daerlun becomes a free city-state after Sembian influence falters due to Cormyrean interference.

The cloaked autocrats known as the Swords of Archendale are discovered to be consorting with Sembia, allowing the dale to counter the subversion by strengthening ties with the other free dales of the Dalelands.
Branwyn Moonsinger, the granddaughter to the late High Queen Alicia Kendrick, is made Great Druid of Sarifal.
The original svirfneblin inhabitants of Blingdenstone begin a decades-long reclamation and rebuilding of their old home under the leadership of Kargien Dissengulp.
The Salty Sails sinks off the Sword Coast, with several casualties.
Kuldhas of Waterdeep publishes A Walk in My City.
Cormyr sends troops from Daerlun and Highcastle to lay siege to Saerb and Urmlaspyr.
Sembia, with the approval of the Netherese, signs the Treaty of Griffonfang Bridge, which ends hostilities with Cormyr, Cormanthor, and the Dalelands. Daerlun and Urmlaspyr gain independence.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 62

events.text: House Huntsilver is wiped out in the war between Cormyr and Sembia. The only two surviving female members marry into House Crownsilver and House Truesilver.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 62

events.text: The Devil You Know: Bryseis Kakistos's story, part eleven.
Prince Foril I of Cormyr goes into battle carrying the ensign of the Purple Dragon, which can only be borne by a true blooded member of House Obarskyr.
King Azoun V ennobles the Goldfeather family, who had twice previously been stripped of their title.
A powerful vampire lord, leading an army of undead, conquers the city of Elturel.
cites: Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus, с. 7

events.text: Banak Brawnanvil, King of Mithral Hall dies. He is succeeded by his son Connerad.
The golemwork clock called Timehands is finally finished in Waterdeep as part of the tallest tower of the Lord's Palace.
This City, Our City ballad by Ondrel Ammandreth performed for the first time in the Castle Ward of Waterdeep.
Crown Prince Irvel Obarskyr of Cormyr marries Ospra Goldfeather, despite pressure from House Crownsilver.
King Azoun V dies.
King Foril Obarskyr inherits the throne of Cormyr from Azoun V.
Auril sends her vassals to battle the djinn and efreet of Calimshan. As a result, the desert of the Skyfire Wastes is frozen over for months.

The Second Era of Skyfire comes to a close in Calimshan as the efreeti Memnon and the djinni Calim mysteriously vanish, presumably to their home plane. However, their followers continue their conflict.
Vasen Cale is born to Varra, who dies in childbirth.
The Godborn begins.

Netheril attempts to establish diplomatic relations with High Imaskar. However, the effort falls apart when a ship given to the Imaskari by the Netherese is attacked by sea monsters and the Netherese abandon the Imaskari crew.
The Shadovar leader Herzgo Alegni applies pressure on Lord Hugo Babris of Neverwinter to have the Winged Wyvern Bridge renamed in his own honor.

A small adventuring party rediscovers the ancient dwarven city of Gauntlgrym. Consisting of Jarlaxle Baenre, Athrogate, and a trio of powerful Thayans, they awaken the ancient primordial Maegera when Korvin Dor'crae hypnotically forces Athrogate to activate the forges.

The Ruining: The city of Neverwinter is destroyed when Mount Hotenow erupts as a result of the awakening of Maegera, a primordial held in slumber through the craftsmanship of the dwarves of Delzoun and the elves of Iliyanbruen at the heart of Gauntlgrym.
All known heirs of the royal House Alagondar die in the eruption of Mount Hotenow. Their spirits haunt Castle Never.
Gauntlgrym (chapters 1-9)
Torimesh the druid returns to Baldur's Gate and creates Insight Park in the district of Brampton.
cites: Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus, с. 189

events.text: A collection of letters written during Lord Charles Blacktree IV's expedition into the Underdark to find the Orb of Protection undertaken in the is uncovered in the ruined Blackwood Manor outside of Ravens Bluff.
The Warlock Knights of Vaasa drive the minotaurs out of Kond.
Tai Shing, the first Suzerain of Thesk, dies, leaving an unstable nest of feuding nobles, merchants and gangs.
Baerovus is born, first son of Crown Prince Irvel Obarskyr and his wife Ospra Goldfeather.
The father of Marod el Arhapan is executed by beheading atop the walls of the palace gardens of Almraiven under orders of Acham el Jhotos.
Three wizards discover the ruins of Saruun Khel beneath Thunderspire Mountain. They found the order of the Mages of Saruun and the Seven-Pillared Hall within the ruins.
Uluin of Merkurn publishes his Annals of Soravia.
cites: The Fall of Highwatch: MMP, с. 1

events.text: Talaric Daoran, despite the agreement between the people of Phlan and the fey of the Quivering Forest, sends loggers into the woods. The next day, he goes missing from Valjevo Castle, never to be seen again.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 170

events.text: In Laerakond, Jada Marlserpent, last surviving member of Clan Marlserpent, is born in the village of Wandering Stones.
cites: Realms of the Dead: Wandering Stones

events.text: The High Observer of Torm ordered the Reaching Woods barricaded, in an attempt to contain the goblin and gnoll tribes living there.
In Laerakond, Clan Marlserpent is decimated by dragons, nearly wiping it out.
cites: Realms of the Dead: Wandering Stones

events.text: Queen Brianne Dragonsbane is assassinated in Bloodstone. This distracts the realm of Bloodstone from the marshalling Vaasan armies in the north. Civil unrest throughout Damara ensues..
Azalar Falconhand resigns lordship of Shadowdale and is succeeded by Addee Ulphor.
The Gentle Ghost of Silverymoon is first sighted in the city.
Raedra Obarskyr is born, the daughter of Crown Prince Irvel Obarskyr of Cormyr and his wife Ospra Goldfeather.
Farideh and Havilar are born and abandoned in the village of of Arush Vayem on the frontier of Tymanther.
The civil war that wracked the Kingdom of Many Arrows finally ends, reuniting the orc tribes under King Obould XVII.
The Warlock Knights of Vaasa go to war with the Kingdom of Bloodstone.
Two devas, Lakini and Lusk, attack and destroy the pirate ship Orcsblood just off the coast of Mulmaster.
Maalthiir of Hillsfar dies in a failed attempt to attain lichdom.
Dawnbringer begins.
The Devil You Know Bryseis Kakistos story, part twelve.
The young mage Jandi M'baren is slain by a former pirate named Helgre at Jadaren Hold.
Dawnbringer
The Slime King, ruler of a derro clan, orders her subjects to abduct a yuan-ti tribe living in the jungle near Delzimmer.

Sylora Salm, a servant of Szass Tam, attempts to repeat the events of a decade previous and cause Mount Hotenow to erupt again. Thankfully for the residents of Neverwinter, she fails when adventurers and a small force of Delzoun dwarves defeat her in Gauntlgrym.
Bruenor Battlehammer dies due to injuries sustained defending Gauntlgrym from a pit fiend.
Thibbledorf Pwent is killed after being stung by the pit fiend Beealtimatuche.
The pureblood yuan-ti later known as Zaltys Serrat is born into a small yuan-ti tribe in the jungles of southern Faerûn.
Demetrios Whitefire of Sossal, High Chillbringer of Auril, pens the Icedawn Syllabus.
cites: Dragon 367: Hall of the Frostmaiden, с. 58

events.text: Gauntlgrym (Ch. 10-epilogue)
The Companions begins.
Venom in Her Veins (Ch. 1-3)
The Shadovar under the command of Herzgo Alegni help defend New Neverwinter against the Thayan zombies and Ashmadai trying to take the city after several assaults.
Neverwintan citizens free their city from Shadovar/Netherese occupation after an assassination attempt on Herzgo Alegni leaves the Netherese leaderless.
The city of Port Llast enjoys a reversal in fortune as the sahuagin who had been plaguing their shores are defeated; a new city wall is erected; and a mass immigration of former Luskars begins.

House Xorlarrin of Menzoberranzan invades Gauntlgrym from below in an attempt to create a sister city, Q'Xorlarrin, free from the absolute rule of House Baenre. They are forced to flee briefly when the Xorlarrin patron Brack'thal Xorlarrin, influenced by Maegera, attempts to set the primordial free, but the drow return immediately after his efforts fail.

Sylora Salm dies at the hands of Jestry Rallevin after she is mortally wounded by the joint effort of Drizzt Do'Urden, Dahlia Sin'felle, and Artemis Entreri. However, Sylora later appears in Thay in 1478 DR, in the home of one of her lieutenants, a vampire named Muthoth.
The Menzoberranyr jeweller Mritt Shadalun is found dead in the vault of his chief rival Hondel Belek'tyr.
Gedrin Thalavar founds the Eye of Justice.
Herzgo Alegni is killed in Gauntlgrym by Dahlia Sin'felle.
Drow wizard Brack'thal Xorlarrin is killed in Gauntlgrym by Artemis Entreri.

The fallen Companions of the Hall, having died and and their souls taken to Mielikki's Iruladoon, are given a second chance by the Forest Queen in order to help their friend and ally, Drizzt Do'Urden. They are reincarnated as newborns, all across Faerûn.
Vidrinath and Orbbcress, the wondrous sword and shield owned by Tiago Baenre, are crafted by Gol'fanin in Gauntlgrym.
Charon's Claw
Neverwinter
The Last Threshold begins
Realms of the Dead
The Resurrection Agent
Samark Dhanzscul becomes the sixth Blackstaff.
Draygo Quick captures Drizzt Do'Urden, believing him to be a Chosen.
Kamoth Kastelmar and Terena Hulmaster are married in Hulburg.
Julen Serrat is born the youngest son of the Guardians branch of the Serrat merchant family.
Ashemmon of Rhymanthiin, the fifth Blackstaff, dies. His essence goes on to reside in Blackstaff Tower alongside his predecessors.
Bregan D'aerthe reestablishes its presence in Luskan, creating a base in the ruins of Illusk beneath the city.

In an attempt to seize control of Griffonwatch Keep in Hulburg, Kamoth Kastelmar and several Shieldsworn loyal to him attempt to kill Harmach Grigor Hulmaster but are discovered. Rather than face prosecution, they flee the castle and town.

The balor lord Errtu and several glabrezu demons attack Bryn Shander in Ten-Towns in an effort to draw out Drizzt Do'Urden. Drizzt does not appear but Tiago Baenre, also hunting Drizzt, witnesses the attack and slays Errtu, banishing him back to the Abyss. Despite their reservations, the people of Bryn Shander laud Tiago as a hero, erecting a statue of him while Drizzt becomes a persona non grata in Ten-towns.
Drizzt Do'Urden, Artemis Entreri, Dahlia Sin'felle, Effron, Ambergris and Afafrenfere are sent into a magical slumber when they discover Iruladoon.
The Scything Wind is burned at sea, with several casualties.
Corsair prologue.

The Tempuswrath occurs. Members of the Order of the Steel Fang are hired to fight on opposing sides of a conflict, and many of the order slay each other in the fighting. Tempus appears before them on the battlefield and commands them to return to proper worship.
City of the Dead begins.
Dagult Neverember arrives in Neverwinter and soon becomes its Lord Protector, a position from which he can begin to rebuild the city.

In the Children's Massacre, all nieces and nephews of Queen Anais Rhindaun of Tethyr are slain in a politically motivated attack, except for her niece Ysabel Linden, who becomes the sole heir to the throne. Evonne Linden, the queen's rebellious half-sister, is killed at the same time in another town. Guardianship of her daughter Ysabel is given to Queen Anais.
Domavos Cormaeril, Lord Morn of Daggerdale, dies and is succeeded by his son, Barathal.
Queen Cyndra of Akanûl dies of illness.
The Warlock Knights of Vaasa raze Bloodstone City, the capital of the unified Kingdom of Bloodstone. The war between the two nations is ended.
Proskur is declared a protectorate of Cormyr to protect it from Netheril..
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: The Jaezred Chaulssin, having infiltrated Menzoberranzan's Arach-Tinilith with sleeper agents over the years, successfully unleash a horde of demons during the Ceremony of Graduation.
Arathane succeeded her mother, the late Queen Cyndra, as the new Queen of Akanûl.
Construction of the Crafthouse of Inspiration, a temple of Gond located east of Eartheart, begins.
Lady Avelyere adopts the Bedine child Ruqiah (Catti-brie) into her coven for young mages in the Shade Enclave.
Velarr, the mysterious wizard who runs the House of Velarr magical school in Zazesspur, disappears after an apparent attack on his school.
cites: Forging the Realms: Newly Fashionable Curses of the Realms

events.text: Members of the Elkannath family abandon Haelond when the mining outpost is overrun by mysterious monsters that swarm out from Laerakond's Underdark.

Anaxims invade the Dominion of the Burned, killing most of its members and forcing the surviving genasi to flee to other regions of Laerakond. A genasi named Brindol rises as the leader of the few Burned who remain in the Dominions of Nehu.
cites: Dragon 375: Gontal: Dominions of Nehu, с. 79

events.text: The Fanged Crown
Borigon, third son of Garumbelly Hillsafar, ascends the throne after thwarting a Warlock Knight invasion of Hillsafar Hall.
The Crafthouse of Inspiration is finished with the assistance of the gold dwarves of Eartheart. During the following years it becomes the most important temple of Gond in the continent.
Eye of Justice prologue.

A rot angel is found in one of the tombs in the Hills of the Dead Kings, and a contingent of halflings from the neighboring villages is sent to dispatch it. Jaeg Felidae, a Malar-worshiping weretiger also hunting the beast, finds the corpses of the halflings that same night. Hours later, he too is dead, having failed to dispatch it.
cites: Realms of the Dead: Feast of the Moon

events.text: A peculiar cache of iron trade bars is unearthed in Flandal's Dell, prompting a group of stern-faced gnomes (rumored to live beneath Kossuth's Ire) to start asking questions in Whitehorn.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 79

events.text: Dungeon #170: "Monument of the Ancients"
Realms of the Dead
Feast of the Moon
Elisa Nettlebee is born to Bertram and Jayne Nettlebee.
Elnantra, Paerevelle, and Ralagondar are born to Skie Silvershield II.
Erlend Brightcovenant is born to Amauntha Bryndfeather and Breszyn Brightcovenant.

Alorae Wanderwyrm is killed by an unknown assailant in Suzail with poison. Witnesses note her last gasping words to be "I die, but fail forever!", though later war wizards speculate if she may have actually said "Fael", referring to the Fael Threl cabal.
cites: Dungeon 183: Eye on the Realms: Circle of Fangs, Part 2, с. 57

events.text: King Emerus Warcrown witnesses an angry Reginald Roundshield in a practice battle and promptly assigns him to Iruladoon's town guard in order to train him and teach him humility.
Brunzarra Hethcanter retires from the office of Lady of Graces in Cormyr's Royal Court. That same year she is succeeded by Lady Jalessa Windstone.

In Delthuntle, the halfling crime lord Grandfather Pericolo Topolino takes an interest in the young boy Regis after seeing him climb a building to escape a gang of much older and larger youths. Dubbing him the "Spider", he goes on to manipulate his father to allow the boy to work for him diving for deep oysters, which Pericolo then cultivates to produce pink pearls. Soon after, Spider is unofficially adopted by Pericolo and trained in the ways of the rogue.
The Companions

The Keepers of the Cerulean Sign attack the Abolethic Sovereignty in Akanûl. In retaliation, the Abolethic Sovereignty destroys Tohrepur, turning its residents into aberrations. The aboleths march this army to the village of Caidris, where they defeat the Keepers' mercenary army and destroy the village.
A storm in Icewind Dale causes a wave on Lac Dinneshere to destroy the docks of Easthaven and several of its ships, as well as their crews.
After an upswing in the faith of Shar in Wheloon, King Foril of Cormyr orders the city sealed and turned into a prison colony.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom

events.text: Avenger begins.
Tarsis, an Oghman priest, is killed by the deva Demascus as part of a plan to cause an Oghman heretic to reveal himself.
Demascus kills the rakshasa Kalkan and is then slain by cultists in Akanûl.
Neranya Cormaeril, sister of the Lord Morn of Daggerdale disappears when her entourage is attacked by werewolves near Castle Daggerdale. Her body is never found.
The Coin Spinners gang of Luskan begin operating a soup kitchen as a front for criminal activity.
Sword of the Gods prologue.

Kalen Dren, the spellscarred follower of the Threefold God known as the heir to Gedrin "Shadowbane" Thalavar, is betrayed by the leadership of the Eye of Justice, an organization once dedicated to the same faith. With the aid of Levia Shadewalker, he fakes his own death and escapes.

All the paladins manning Fort Morninglord, west of Elturel, disappear one night under mysterious circumstances that leave every stone of the keep blackened and every window and door fused. Soon after, the High Observer of Torm forbids entrance to the keep.

The Mask Dance, an erotic dance in which the dancer wears nothing but a mask, takes Suzail by storm. This form of entertainment becomes so popular that it soon spreads to other major cities, notably Westgate.
The herbalist Janesse Wyndsur begins selling Spellslayer wine, a concoction that renders mages unable to cast spells for several hours.
cites: Dungeon 195: Eye on the Realms: Spellslayer Wine

events.text: During a tournament between the defenders of Myth Drannor, Geran Hulmaster and Rhovann Disarnnyl, both contenders for the love of the moon elf maiden Alliere, fight a duel that ends when Geran cuts off his opponent's hand. This prompts his banishment from Myth Drannor.
King Mith, the King of Iltkazar, is restored to life, having had his astral form stolen by Tiamat a full century previously.
The tiefling Farideh unintentionally makes a warlock pact with the cambion Lorcan.
The young Cormyran noble Aubrin Crownsilver flees a Tormite monastery for the Sword Coast.
Emrius Baergil becomes Captain of the Riders of Mistledale, aged 22.
cites: Candlekeep forum: Questions for Ed Greenwood (2011): Captain Baergil

events.text: An earthquake strikes northern Vaasa and Damara, which causes Castle Perilous to shed its crumbling exterior and reveal a new, sleek black stone underneath.
The Great Port of Tarmalune, which until now was unwalled, completes construction of a gated wall.
The Dragonriders' Club, an expensive, risqué dancing club opens in Suzail.
Swordmage prologue.
Brimstone Angels prologue

A casting of the legendary spell Tarchamus' volcano causes a freak eruption in the Nether Mountains, leading ash and rock to rain across the High Forest as well as creating a plume of smoke so large that it was visible from Waterdeep.

The exiled Thayan Zulkirs lead their army into Thay accompanied by Aoth Fezim's Brotherhood of the Griffon and Bareris Anskuld in an attempt to stop Szass Tam's plan to destroy the multiverse and build it anew as he sees fit.

After defeating Szass Tam, Aoth Fezim leads the Brotherhood of the Griffon into Impiltur to fight a demon-worshiping cult. The Brotherhood is betrayed by a noble and is forced to retreat, later finding employment in Chessenta.

With his plot to achieve godhood having failed, Szass Tam nominally reestablishes the Council of Zulkirs to handle day-to-day governance of Thay. He fills the Council solely with his faithful lackeys, but Thayan politicking inevitably resumes.
Glasya, Archduchess of the Sixth Layer of the Nine Hells, attempts a convoluted plot to bring her father Asmodeus into conflict with the Abolethic Sovereignty in Neverwinter.

Lord Dagult Neverember, the self-proclaimed Lord Protector of Neverwinter, issues a standing order that anyone in the city showing signs of Spellplague infection should be sent to Helm's Hold for treatment.
Neverember's spymaster, Dhafiyand, is revealed to be an agent of the Red Wizards of Thay when he attempts but fails to assassinate the Lord Protector.
The erinyes Invadiah is demoted to succubus form and her cambion son Lorcan is imprisoned in Malbolge as punishment for screwing up one of the archdevil Glasya's plots in Neverwinter.
The dragon Brimstone draws the draconic rulers of Murghôm into a game of Xorvintaal.
The Brotherhood of the Griffon turn against the Simbarchs of Aglarond.
Gregor receives a vision and convinces one of the largest monasteries of Kelemvor to move from Impiltur to Ormpetarr.
A group of adventurers led by the Harper Tam Zawad vie with Shades and the Zhentarim to find the lost Library of Tarchamus and plunder its treasures. Unfortunately the library is destroyed.
The tiefling Kylynne Silmerhelve joins the Black Robes

Lallara Mediocros (Thay's Zulkir of Abjuration), Malark Springhill, Samas Kul (Thay's Zulkir of Transmutation), Bareris Anskuld, Nevron (Thay's Zulkir of Conjuration), and Lauzoril (Thay's Zulkir of Enchantment) die fighting Szass Tam.
Tarchamus the Unyielding's undead form is destroyed by Farideh and friends at Xammux.
Shadow creatures begin appearing at random throughout eastern Cormanthor and attack travelers.
Brimstone Angels (except prologue)
Lesser Evils
Cold Steel and Secrets
The Adversary begins.
The Captive Flame begins.
Unholy
The green dragon Skuthosiin sends his forces of ash giants to invade Tymanther.
Lendris, a small town outside Baldur's Gate, is terrorized for a tenday by a mysterious undead warrior.
cites: Realms of the Dead: The Bone Bird

events.text: Tchazzar, the lost king of Chessenta, returns to his kingdom. Rescued by members of the Brotherhood of the Griffon

Shala Karanok cedes her title of War-hero of Chessenta to Tchazzar. The dragon proclaims his own divinity, ordering a grand temple to his worship be erected. He also lifts the nationwide ban on wizards.
A dust wight known as Dusty Bones is briefly freed from a crypt in the City of the Dead in Waterdeep before being recaptured by the ghostly warrior Ash and the maintenance worker Leaplow Carver.
cites: Realms of the Dead: Dusty Bones

events.text: Chessentan forces are victorious against Threskelan interlopers in Soolabax.
Tymantheran forces are victorious against the giant invaders.
The ancient green dragon Skuthosiin is slain by dragonborn knights of Tymanther.
Tchazzar destroys the physical form of the ancient bone wyrm Alasklerbanbastos.
Nala, a priestess of Tiamat is slain in a battle at Ashhold.

The small village of Wandering Stones in the mountains bordering Skelkor and the Sword Lands is attacked by the brown dragon Thovantareth. The spirit of the primordial Arumbar manifests to defend the town.
cites: Realms of the Dead: Wandering Stones

events.text: Samark Dhanzscul, the sixth Blackstaff, is slain by Khondar "Ten-Rings" Naomal and his son, Centiv.
Vajra Safahr becomes the seventh Blackstaff, and announces it to Waterdeep at dawn. She chooses Laraelra Harsard as her heir.
Khondar Naomal is slain while attempting to breach the defences of Ahghairon's Tower.

Renaer Neverember, along with his friends Laraelra Harsard, Torlyn Wands, Osco Salibuck, Meloon Wardragon, Eiruk Weskur, Harug Shieldsunder, Palek Lateriff, and with the support of the new Blackstaff, Vajra Safahr, revives the Moonstars for the betterment of Waterdeep.
The Northwall Deathhouse in Dagger Falls is discovered to be haunted by the spirit of a deadly Zhentarim spy named Vathris Koll.
cites: Realms of the Dead: A Prayer for Brother Robert

events.text: Chessenta defeats Threskel in a brief war and claims Threskel as a vassal kingdom.
Chessenta erupts into a brief civil war in which the Brotherhood of the Griffon, Akanûl and Chessentan forces loyal to Shala Karanok defeat Tchazzar's forces.

A horde of orcs, hobgoblins, and ogres, bolstered by a group of Warlock Knights and controlled monsters, destroys the small mining town of Glister. Hoping to accomplish the same at Hulburg, they are narrowly defeated by an army half their size, consisting of human, dwarven, and undead warriors, at the Battle of Lendon's Dike.

The ruins of Tethgard are the site of a bloody battle between the trio of Elminster, Storm Silverhand, and the Simbul against a company of War Wizards and Purple Dragons seeking to take them into custody.

Treth Halonter and Relve Langral - former members of the Nine turned into blueflame ghosts by Myrkul - butcher their way through Suzail, hunting a noble at the command of Marlin Stormserpent, slaying dozens.
Manshoon, having covertly eliminated Elminster's contingency spells over a period of months, finally manages to destroy the Sage of Shadowdale.
Many of the traitorous nobles imprisoned in Castle Irlingstar are slain in Rorskryn Mreldrake's refinements of a spell to harden air into a weapon. The castle is abandoned.

Several magically-dominated nobles are slain killing Lady Marantine Delcastle in Manshoon's attempt to get at Elminster. He is successful, and when Elminster calls him out, the Old Sage is nearly destroyed in the ensuing battle between himself, Manshoon's death tyrants, and Suzail's War Wizards. He is saved only by the timely arrival of the Simbul, who sacrifices herself by restoring the Old Sage to his original body and giving him her silver fire.

Enraged at the death of his paramour and the countless others slain by Manshoon's machinations, and with a painful overabundance of Mystra's silver fire, Elminster tracks down and destroys Manshoon's body. In the process, he discovers that Manshoon is himself a Chosen of Mystra and that he does not have power enough to kill him.
A large force from Ravens Bluff led by Myrkyssa Jelan defeats the drow of House Chumavh in the Underdark beneath the city.
Tarmel Drouth, the exiled bastard son of Rancelair Illance of House Illance of Cormyr, attacks his father and grandfather at the family's summer home at Stag Well although both men survive.
cites: Dungeon 176: Eye on the Realms: Tarmel Drouth, Outcast Noble

events.text: The Hillborn Dwarves recapture the Fireguard Fortress on Mount Hotenow in the Neverwinter Woods from Ignazar and the Cult of Maegera.
Much of the Dread Ring in Neverwinter woods is destroyed by the coalition led by Alphonse Knox.
During the Battle of Luthcheq, Tchazzar is killed by Shala Karanok and Alasklerbanbastos' physical form is destroyed for the second time in the same year.
Halonya, the high priestess of the Cult of Tchazzar is killed by priests of Tiamat.
Pasha Marod el Arhapan, the ruler of Calimport, is killed by his son Cephas.
The ranger Mattias Farseer and his pet wyvern Trill are killed fighting a demon in the Plain of Stone Spiders.
The demon Murmur and his compatriot Kalkan are killed by the deva Demascus
Vraith, the leader of the Order of Blue Flame in Ormpetarr has her soul joined with the magical border of the Plaguewrought Land.
The rogue Duvan dies during experiments conducted by the Order of Blue Flame but is later resurrected by a high priestess of Kelemvor.
Slanya, a Kelemvoran monk dies preventing the Order of Blue Flame from completing the Ritual of the Border.
The exiled eladrin Caelynna is slain by the monk Kwan Shang-Li
Shestandeliath Patrin, a dragonborn paladin of Bahamut is slain in a duel with a paladin of Torm, Daardendrien Medrash.
Lord Khault, the leader of a cult in Tohrepur known as The Choir, is slain by the Half-elf Brindani.
The Half-elf hero Brindani dies during a battle against Lord Khault and other members of The Choir.
Marlin Stormserpent, a young noble from Suzail is slain by Cymmarraa who wanted the Blueflame items he possessed.
Natan, the shadar-kai high priest of Tempus in Ikemmu is murdered by Vedoran.
Vedoran is killed by the young Shadar-kai warrior Ashok
Chanoch, a young Shadar-kai warrior, is executed by Uwan for insubordination.
Symrustar Auglamyr, having been a captive of the drow since before the Spellplague, finally dies from the tortures and experiments inflicted upon her to steal the silver fire of Mystra within her.
The drow Marquise Dresimil Chumavh is killed by Myrkyssa Jelan in the Underdark beneath Ravens Bluff.
The slaver Fetterfist is killed by Jack Ravenwild
The dragonborn guard captain Krailash dies pushing the derro Slime King through a portal to the Far Realm.

Having absorbed too much silver fire from the Simbul and Manshoon, Elminster flees to Mystra and returns a large part of her divinity to her, returning a goddess of magic to the Realms. This event becomes known as Mystra's Return.

The apprentice wizard Tennora Hedare and a Blue dragon in human form named Clytemorrenestrix foil a plot by Andareunarthex, a young Green dragon, to bypass the dragon wards and establish himself as a power in Waterdeep.

Elminster, though having had his body destroyed, survives as some sort of magical ash. With the aid of Storm Silverhand, he transfers his essence to Amarune Whitewave, a descendant of his who agrees to share her body while the Sage of Shadowdale trains her.
Mirt the Moneylender is released from his decades long imprisonment in a Blueflame axe by Marlin Stormserpent.
The Simbul is restored to sanity by Elminster and Storm when they feed her a Blueflame item.
The yuan-ti pureblood Zaltys Serrat attempts to rescue her birth tribe from derro in the Underdark.
Ruqiah (Catti-brie) flees Lady Avelyere's coven in the Shade Enclave and is taken in by the Harpells of Longsaddle.
Reginald Roundshield (Bruenor Battlehammer) travels to Mithral Hall as a caravan guard.
Myth Drannor and New Velar form an alliance in opposition to Netheril.
The Cult of the Elder Elemental Eye re-emerges in Akanûl but is destroyed in the same year by Demascus.

links.t: Cult of the Elder Elemental Eye

events.text: The Firestorm Cabal in Airspur is infiltrated by the Cult of the Elder Elemental Eye but survives when the cult is destroyed.
The Order of Blue Flame attempts to move the border of the Plaguewrought Land but is foiled by Duvan and Tyrangal.
The Brotherhood of the Griffon thwarts Tchazzar's plan to invade Tymanther and leads rebel forces to a victory over Tchazzar's army.
The Choir kidnaps a number of residents from Airspur and takes them to its shrine in Tohrepur. The Choir is later destroyed by Uthalion and friends.

Cormyr's top two war wizards, Ganrahast and Vainrence are placed into magical stasis by the Death knight Targrael and entombed in the palace crypt. They are later revived by Elminster and Vangerdahast's shade.
The temple of Beshaba in Ikemmu attempts to start a revolt against Uwan's rule.
Drow from Menzoberranzan attempt to steal Araknul's arambarium ore supply.
House Serrat of Delzimmer loses one of its primary sources of income when a portal to the Far Realm through which terazul plants grew is sealed.
An earthquake strikes the Delhalls mine in Vaasa, which causes the entrance to collapse. Once it reopens, mysterious new caverns filled with haunting music are discovered.
This is the year of the "present" in the fourth edition Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide and the Forgotten Realms Player's Guide.
Daranthur's Hall in Athkatla is seriously damaged and dozens of traders are killed when bottles of adulterated wine react to spells cast by Amaront of Selgaunt.
cites: Dragon 407: Eye on the Realms: A Surprising Vintage
